After the SFT warm-up, we continue alignment with the remaining data using RL driven by process-based rewards. We set the model’s maximum context length to 11K tokens, with the input length capped at 10K, which constitutes a typical ultra-long sequence optimization setting. Therefore, we enable the DAPO loss for process-reward alignment within a GRPO framework. We perform credit assignment via token-level policy gradients, and mitigate entropy collapse by decoupling the clipping range from dynamic sampling constraints, ensuring that the within-group advantage retains non-zero variance. This makes the method better suited to long-chain reasoning and structured operation-sequence generation. In addition, by limiting the maximum generation length and applying dynamic resampling to filter degenerate groups, we reduce training noise introduced by truncation and within-group advantage degeneration.
